Before the 2004 quake there were three arguments against a large earthquake occurring in the Sumatra region. After the quake it was considered that earthquake hazard risk would need to be reassessed for regions previously thought to have low risk based on these criteria:[[59]](#cite_note-60)

1. The subducting plate at the location of the 2004 quake is older and more dense. Before the 2004 earthquake it was thought that only the subduction of young and buoyant crust could produce giant earthquakes.
2. Slow plate motion. Previously it was thought that the convergence rate had to be fast.
3. Before the 2004 quake it was thought that giant earthquakes only occurred in regions without [back-arc basins](/wiki/Back-arc_basin "Back-arc basin").

Dwight D. Eisenhower :: Post-presidency (1961–1969) :: Death :: chunk_0045
At 12:25 p.m. on March 28, 1969, Eisenhower died from [congestive heart failure](/wiki/Congestive_heart_failure "Congestive heart failure") at [Walter Reed Army Medical Center](/wiki/Walter_Reed_Army_Medical_Center "Walter Reed Army Medical Center") in Washington, D.C., at age 78. His last words were: "I've always loved my wife, my children, and my grandchildren, and I've always loved my country. I want to go. God, take me."[[279]](#cite_note-281) The following day, his body was moved to the [Washington National Cathedral](/wiki/Washington_National_Cathedral "Washington National Cathedral")'s Bethlehem Chapel, where he lay in repose for 28 hours.[[280]](#cite_note-FinalPost-282) He was then transported to the [United States Capitol](/wiki/United_States_Capitol "United States Capitol"), where he [lay in state](/wiki/Lying_in_state#United_States "Lying in state") in the [Capitol Rotunda](/wiki/Capitol_Rotunda "Capitol Rotunda") on March 30 and 31.[[281]](#cite_note-283) A [state funeral](/wiki/State_funeral "State funeral") was conducted at the Washington National Cathedral on March 31.[[282]](#cite_note-Funeral-284) The president and first lady, Richard and Pat Nixon, attended, as did former president Lyndon B. Johnson. Former President Harry S. Truman was unable to attend due to a vacation.
